LENS

Learnable Edge Network Sparsification for Interpretable Histopathology

Demo Explore Method Results Code

TL;DR

LENS learns which edges of a slide graph to keep. Every edge gets a Hard-Concrete gate, and an L0 penalty closes the gates that do not help. The model keeps about 30% of the edges and still classifies well. The edges that survive show which tissue it relied on.

The animation behind this page follows the same path as the method: patches, graph, edge weights, then sparsity. Scroll and watch it change.

Method

Graph from patches
A slide is tiled at 20×. UNI2-h turns each patch into a 1536-number vector (SimCLR ResNet18 gives 512). Each patch links to its 8 nearest neighbors by position.
Learnable edge gates
An edge scoring network gives each edge a Hard-Concrete gate. Temperature anneals from 5.0 to 0.67 on a cosine schedule. An L0 penalty pushes gates toward zero. γ = −0.1 ζ = 1.1 β = 0.66
Penalty schedule
The penalty weight rises linearly through warmup (epochs 0 to 15), ramps to twice its base value (15 to 35), then holds.
Density control
A density loss aims to keep 30% of the edges. The penalty is scaled by a factor that grows when the graph is denser than the target. λ_eff = α · λ₀ α = clip(1 + (ρ − ρ*), 0.2, 2.0)

Results

LENS keeps about 30% of the graph edges and stays discriminative. It was benchmarked on CPTAC and checked on several TCGA cohorts.

  • CPTAC
  • TCGA-BRCA
  • TCGA-RCC
  • TCGA-LUAD
  • TCGA-LUSC

Testing reports bootstrap confidence intervals for the ROC and PR curves. The heatmap script paints the learned edge weights over the slide, red for strongly connected tissue and blue for weakly connected tissue.
